maya: Heads-up — since the 03:00 deploy we're seeing a 2-3x latency tail on Dedicated GPUs when speculative decoding pairs Llama-3-draft -> Mixtral-base. Mostly observed on seq_len>1024 workloads. Profiling points at kernel churn and KV-cache thrash.

sam: repro steps? is this only with batching or even batch=1?

maya: repro on local perf rig with batch=1 and batch=8. Batch=8 amplifies the tail but batch=1 still shows ~40% tail increase vs yesterday.

maya: quick profiler dump (high level):
```
kernel_selector: heavy hop count (switching kernels per layer)
GPU matmul_small_kernel: 62%
KV cache evictions/s: 74
spec_decision_accept_rate: 0.14 (expected ~0.6 for this draft pairing)
roPE_scale_applied: mixtral scaled -> 1.8x relative to host LLAMA config
```

leo: that roPE scaling jump worries me — if tokenizers don't align, kv keys might not be reused and cache becomes useless. Also kernel selector may be picking head-specialized kernels because model meta implies different head dim.

anya: I noticed the draft and target model families have mismatched head dims in our catalog: llm-llama/3-draft -> heads=64, mixtral->heads=48 in model metadata. Our kernel selector currently picks fused-qkv for heads % 48 == 0; fallback to generic matmul otherwise. Means we see kernel churn when the draft hints at one shape then the target uses another.

sam: can we gate speculative pairing earlier based on family compatibility? e.g., require head/kdim match and tokenization alias before enabling drafts. Quick mitigation: disable speculative pairing for pairings with head_dim mismatch.

devx: agreed for short-term. Long-term we want a compatibility matrix and a soft-fallback where the runtime rewrites the draft's metadata to a compatible view rather than brute disabling. This avoids latency cliff.

maya: experiment results: forcing kernel_selector to prefer generic fused kernel reduced kernel churn but acceptance stayed low. Means we're still losing on spec acceptance because tokenizer mismatch + rope scaling.

infra-bot: perf-harness started: redwood-bench run --pair llama3-draft:mixtral-base --batch 8 --kv-profile --dump-traces -> /tmp/run-1891122334.log

leo: suggestion: two parallel experiments
- A: apply family gating (strict) -> expect acceptance rate to stay low but latency tail drops (no speculative overhead)
- B: runtime metadata remap + force qkv-fused kernel -> hope acceptance improves if kv keys align

anya: tokenizer mapping option: add an alias mapping on the draft side that normalizes byte-level offsets to the target's tokenizer. Quick hack: transform draft token ids via token_map at pairing time for first N prefix tokens. Could bump acceptance but risk hallucination drift.

sam: acceptance tuning knobs to try:
- reduce draft_max_tokens from 64 -> 16 for mixed-family pairing
- increase spec_accept_threshold from 0.5 -> 0.75 (more conservative)
- enable lightweight prefix-KV canonicalization for first 32 tokens

maya: microbench data (after forcing generic kernel, before tokenizer hack):
```
batch=1: p50 28ms -> 33ms, p95 110ms -> 240ms (regression)
batch=8: p50 160ms -> 220ms, p95 720ms -> 1700ms (huge tail)
spec_accept_rate: 0.14 -> unchanged
kv_evictions: 74/s -> 12/s (so kernel fix helped cache pressure but still low spec acceptance)
```

devx: interesting — kernel change lowered evictions but didn't help acceptance. So the root is token/rope mismatch leading to divergent KV keys and low draft acceptance.

leo: action idea: add a lightweight roPE-scale check on pairing: compute a cheap fingerprint of prefix queries across models (e.g., hash of first-layer KV outputs) to estimate reuse probability before enabling speculative path. If reuse_p < 0.5, refuse pairing. This avoids worst-case tails.

anya: can implement fingerprint quickly in runtime as a 1-2ms check per request using cached prefix features. I'll prototype.

sam: short-term PRs:
- sam: disable speculative pairing for head_dim mismatch (PR#4021)
- leo: add kernel-selector preference flag to force fused-qkv on pairing (PR#4023)
- anya: prototype tokenizer alias mapping and reuse fingerprint (WIP)
- maya: run exhaustive perf harness and collect traces for the next 24h (owner of the issue)

maya: one more note on tradeoffs: making spec_accept_threshold stricter reduces false-accepts (bad outputs) and reduces wasted token compute but increases latency if we disable spec path; customers relying on high-throughput short-latency may prefer strict gating. We should expose a policy per tenant.

devx: agreed — expose pairing_policy: {strict, permissive, auto} in tenant config. Default to 'auto' which runs fingerprint check.

infra-bot: run summary uploaded: /tmp/run-1891122334.log -> 1891124400 (will auto-delete in 7d)

maya: ok assigning tasks in GH: sam -> #4021, leo -> #4023, anya -> #4024 (fingerprint + token_map prototype), maya -> #4025 (perf harness + trace collation).

maya: tentative rollback window if we see customer impact: schedule canary revert at 1891126000. Ping me if any urgent regressions. :warning:

sam: thanks, will open PRs and link perf numbers.

leo: I'll also add a short doc in eng-runtime/README about pairing compatibility heuristics and kernel selector caveats.

anya: WIP patch will log a pairing-confidence score in traces so we can correlate acceptance vs fingerprint.

maya: cool. If we can get a quick patch that blocks the worst pairings, we should mitigate the tail for now.

devx: TL;DR: root cause appears to be tokenization + RoPE scale mismatch leading to KV divergence; kernel selection amplifies churn. Short-term: gate by head_dim and add fingerprint check. Medium-term: runtime metadata remap + tokenizer aliasing + tenant policy.

maya: thanks all — will post follow-ups after the 24h run. :coffee:
